video.title: The Most Profitable AI Business You've Never Heard Of

summary: Chris Koerner demonstrates using Claude with Beehiiv’s MCP to connect a newsletter list to a community and find engaged subscribers. He then pitches an AI-assisted service that helps business owners reactivate their email lists and generate sales, using a landscaping example to model potential returns. The video also explains community launch tactics, suggests starting a local newsletter from an existing customer list, and shows Beehiiv community features. Its central business case relies on hypothetical conversion and revenue assumptions, and Koerner discloses an affiliate link and discount for Beehiiv.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office; demonstrates Beehiiv and Claude and pitches AI-assisted newsletter monetization.

ideas.name: AI-assisted email list reactivation and monetization service
ideas.one_liner: Help businesses use their existing email lists to identify engaged past customers and generate repeat sales, using AI and email-platform tools.
ideas.business_model: Monthly retainer, potentially with payment contingent on revenue generated.
ideas.customer: Business owners with existing email lists, including home-service businesses such as landscapers and plumbers.
ideas.problem: Their lists may be large but disconnected from other products, poorly segmented, or not used to generate repeat business.
ideas.offer: Connect or import a client's list into Beehiiv, inspect engagement and subscriber data, create useful segments, and prepare or send campaigns to invite engaged past customers to buy again.

pricing.model: Suggested monthly retainer; Koerner also suggests a no-risk arrangement where the client pays only if revenue is generated.
pricing.notes: The $1,000 monthly retainer and no-risk arrangement are suggestions, not results from a demonstrated client engagement.

acquisition_channels.details: Start with business owners the founder already knows, offer to manage their list, and ask satisfied clients to refer peers.

quote.text: But most importantly, you need to manage the email list of people you know and help them make more money with it.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Koerner suggests posting in Facebook groups for local communities to reach business owners; he gives no specific post or response data.

quote.text: You can use ads. You can post in Facebook groups to local communities. Post on Reddit, yada yada yada.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Koerner also suggests ads and Reddit posts to reach business owners who are not already known to the founder; no specific campaign process is provided.

quote.text: You can use ads. You can post in Facebook groups to local communities. Post on Reddit, yada yada yada.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.delivery: Use Claude connected to Beehiiv through its MCP to inspect list data, rank subscribers, create segments, and prepare or send email invitations. The operator or client still needs to decide what to offer, approve consequential messages, and may call highly engaged subscribers personally.
unit_economics_claims: Koerner models a landscaping list of 20,000 subscribers, with half treated as inactive and 40% of the remainder opening emails, yielding 4,000 active subscribers.
His hypothetical assumes a 0.1% monthly conversion rate, four projects per month at $3,000 each, or $12,000 monthly revenue before costs.
He suggests charging $1,000 per month and describes the hypothetical return as 12x, without substantiating the conversion or revenue assumptions.

acquisition.how: Client acquisition is described as relying on relationships, referrals, groups, ads, and posts. In the UK, software-led unsolicited marketing to individuals and sole traders is constrained by PECR; cold email to limited companies and screened cold calls require care.

onboarding.how: AI can guide a client through exporting a CSV, importing a list, and connecting the platform, with routine human review of access and data permissions.

delivery.how: Agents can inspect engagement, create segments, and draft campaigns, but a person should verify data, claims, consent, and campaign content before sending.

billing.how: A recurring retainer can be invoiced automatically; the suggested pay-only-on-results arrangement would need human review of attribution and revenue.

support.how: AI can answer routine platform questions, but client coordination, offer decisions, and interpretation of results need regular human input.

uk_applicability.notes: The email-list service concept transfers, but UK GDPR and PECR affect list permissions and marketing. Existing consent and the distinction between corporate subscribers and individuals or sole traders matter; the video does not discuss UK rules.

risks: The example's list size, open rate, conversion rate, project value, and resulting revenue are hypothetical assumptions, not demonstrated client results.
A client may not have valid permission to use its list for the proposed campaign; check lawful basis, privacy information, and opt-outs before processing or sending.
The video's AI demonstrations do not establish that an agent will reliably interpret list data or send the right campaign without human review.
The proposed no-risk, pay-only-on-results arrangement could create disputes about attribution and what counts as revenue generated.

ideas.name: AI-assisted newsletter-to-community setup service
ideas.one_liner: Set up or revive a client's Beehiiv community alongside its newsletter and help seed early member activity.
ideas.business_model: Service fees for configuring and launching a client's community; ongoing management pricing is not stated.
ideas.customer: Newsletter owners and small-business owners who have an email list but no active community attached to it.
ideas.problem: A community may exist but be empty, hard to understand, or disconnected from the newsletter and its readers.
ideas.offer: Use an AI assistant and Beehiiv to clarify the community's identity, suggest conversation starters, select initial members, create segments, and configure onboarding and channels.

pricing.notes: The video pitches helping clients but gives no setup or management fee.

acquisition_channels.details: Offer the service to a newsletter owner or business owner already known to the founder; Koerner frames the plumbing-business owner friend as an example.

quote.text: And this video is going to show you how to get paid to do for them what I'm about to do for myself.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: The service can be pitched to people who already own a newsletter or email list, including people reached through the operator's own audience.

quote.text: Way number one, you already have an email list. Way number two, and honestly this is probably the bigger opportunity, you know someone who has a list.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.delivery: Connect the client's Beehiiv account to Claude through the MCP or work directly in Beehiiv. Configure the community, write its description and prompts, identify initial members from list engagement data, and set up onboarding. The owner or operator should actively reply to early posts and invite highly engaged readers.

acquisition.how: Koerner describes finding clients through personal relationships and existing audiences. Automated unsolicited contact to UK individuals and sole traders is constrained by PECR.

onboarding.how: The MCP and AI can help configure the account and onboarding flow, but a human needs access approval and should check the client's community setup.

delivery.how: AI can draft descriptions, prompts, and setup plans, but seeding participation and replying to early members requires active human involvement.

billing.how: A fixed service fee could be collected through recurring or one-off invoicing software, though the video describes no billing setup.

support.how: AI can suggest responses and moderation guidance, but an operator needs to sustain early engagement and handle member issues.

uk_applicability.notes: The service model can transfer to UK newsletter owners. Confirm the platform's suitability for the client's needs and handle member data and communications under UK privacy and marketing rules.

risks: The host says communities have a two-sided chicken-and-egg problem: readers need writers and members need reasons to engage.
A community that looks inactive may deter new members.
Early community engagement is labor-intensive; Koerner recommends replying to every comment during the initial period.
The video has an affiliate relationship with Beehiiv, which may influence the product recommendation.

ideas.delivery: Operate a community platform with channels, a feed, messages, events, onboarding emails, and optional gamification. The owner or community manager needs to create an active environment, encourage discussion, and keep members returning.

acquisition.how: Newsletter, social, and video content can attract members through inbound channels, but an audience and ongoing promotion are still needed.

onboarding.how: The platform can send welcome messages, add members to segments, and trigger email flows automatically.

delivery.how: Software can host posts and events, but community value depends on people contributing and an owner encouraging engagement.

billing.how: Paid access may be administered by the platform, though payment setup and any exceptions need human oversight.

support.how: AI can help with routine questions, but moderation, relationship building, and member conflicts require human attention.

uk_applicability.notes: Online communities are workable in the UK. Pricing, privacy, consumer terms, and platform availability should be checked for the specific community.

risks: Communities need both readers and writers; low participation can make the product feel inactive.
The host recommends starting with a small number of useful channels and removing inactive ones after observing participation.
The video presents community learning as a growing opportunity but offers no evidence for its broad claim that traditional education is declining.

ideas.problem: A service-business list may contain people in the same area who could benefit from local information and a shared community.
ideas.offer: Help a plumbing business owner launch a local newsletter from the business's list and potentially connect it to a community.

pricing.notes: No advertising, subscription, or service pricing is described.

acquisition_channels.details: Start from the business owner's existing email list and its knowledge of subscribers' locations.

quote.text: So what's stopping you from helping your plumbing business owner friend from launching a local newsletter off the back of his email list?

ideas.delivery: The operator would create and send a local newsletter using the existing list; Koerner suggests connecting it to a community but does not describe the editorial workflow or who would write it.

acquisition.how: An existing, permissioned local list can provide an initial audience. Growing beyond it would require inbound content or other channels not detailed in the video.

onboarding.how: Email platform tools can import and segment subscribers, but list permissions, location data, and invitation copy need review.

delivery.how: AI can help draft and schedule newsletter content, but local accuracy and editorial choices need human checks.

billing.how: The video does not describe a revenue model or billing process; any future subscriptions or sponsorships would need setup and oversight.

support.how: AI can answer routine questions, but local community interaction and corrections need human oversight.

uk_applicability.notes: Local newsletters can work in UK towns and cities. The list owner must have a suitable basis to use customer data for newsletter communications, and any local claims should be accurate.

risks: A plumbing customer list was collected for a business purpose and may not be suitable for an unrelated local newsletter without appropriate permissions.
The transcript does not explain how the newsletter would earn revenue or how editorial work would be funded.

ideas.one_liner: Start a newsletter, then invite subscribers into a community when they are most engaged.
ideas.business_model: Newsletter-supported community; whether the newsletter or community is free, paid, or sponsor-funded is not stated.
ideas.customer: A niche audience interested in a topic the publisher covers.
ideas.problem: A new publisher needs a lower-friction way to build an audience before asking people to join a community.
ideas.offer: Publish a newsletter and use the subscriber relationship to invite readers to a related community, especially when they first subscribe.

pricing.notes: The host recommends starting with a newsletter before a community but does not describe newsletter pricing or monetization.

acquisition_channels.details: Koerner describes his own audience as coming from social media and YouTube, among other sources; no particular growth method is supplied.

quote.text: Members come from everywhere. My podcast, social, YouTube, email, Instagram, they're all separate streams that I have to figure out a way to manage.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Koerner cites YouTube as one source of his own audience but gives no subscriber-acquisition results for a new newsletter.

quote.text: Members come from everywhere. My podcast, social, YouTube, email, Instagram, they're all separate streams that I have to figure out a way to manage.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.delivery: Write and send a newsletter, then invite subscribers to a related community. The video does not explain the newsletter's editorial process or how it would be monetized.

acquisition.how: Search, video, and social content can bring subscribers inbound, but audience growth requires publishing and promotion.

onboarding.how: Newsletter software can automate welcome emails and community invitations.

delivery.how: AI can assist with drafting and sending, but editorial judgment and factual checks remain important.

billing.how: The video gives no newsletter revenue or billing model to automate.

support.how: AI can help with common subscriber questions, but a publisher still needs to respond to readers and manage the community.

risks: A newsletter does not automatically turn into revenue; the host says it needs to be used effectively.
A community is a higher-friction invitation than a newsletter, so conversion may be limited if readers are not engaged.

tactics.name: Start with a warm client
steps: List business owners you already know who have email lists.
Offer to help them use the list to generate repeat business.
Consider a no-risk fee structure where payment is due only after measurable revenue is generated.
Ask a satisfied client to introduce you to other business owners.

quote.text: But most importantly, you need to manage the email list of people you know and help them make more money with it.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Find and segment engaged subscribers
steps: Import the client's historical list data where available.
Use engagement, geography, tenure, acquisition source, and purchase status to identify useful subscriber groups.
Create a segment of highly engaged subscribers before sending an invitation or offer.
Ask the client to personally call the strongest prospects where appropriate.

quote.text: And then I'm going to have to do number two and three because I think those are important as well and are not a very big lift.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Estimate a repeat-purchase campaign
steps: Estimate how many subscribers are still active.
Apply an explicit conversion assumption to the engaged group.
Multiply the expected customers by the claimed average project value to estimate gross revenue.
Label the result as revenue, not profit, and verify assumptions with a real client campaign before promising an outcome.

quote.text: That's $12,000 a month in revenue, not profit.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Seed a community with likely participants
steps: Select 10 to 20 highly engaged people as founding members.
Make the community's purpose obvious at a glance.
Give new members a simple first assignment and provide a few low-pressure conversation starters.
Reply to every comment during the first 14 days.

quote.text: Seed 10 to 20 founding members by hand. Now, those have to be very like super fans, highly engaged people.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Keep community structure small and active
steps: Start with three or four channels, or test a few more if the right categories are unclear.
Observe which channels get activity.
After a month or three, reduce the structure to the two or three channels members use most.
Add one recurring weekly ritual with the same post on the same day.

quote.text: So you might even want to add five to six channels and then just know in a month or three you're going to cut that down to two to three, the ones that are the most active
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Use the newsletter-to-community moment
steps: Treat the newsletter as the lower-friction first product.
Invite subscribers to the community when they first join the newsletter.
Give the invitation a clear explanation of the community's purpose.

quote.text: But remember, the most likely time a newsletter subscriber would ever even want to think about your community is the second they subscribe to your newsletter.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Use AI to explore subscriber data and platform actions
steps: Connect the email platform's MCP to the selected AI tool.
Ask it to explain the list import process if the client is new to the platform.

warnings.warning: The central $12,000 revenue example is hypothetical and explicitly described as revenue, not profit; the conversion rate and project value are assumptions.
Koerner says a community can fail when it looks inactive and emphasizes the difficulty of getting both readers and writers to participate.
Koerner recommends replying to every comment for the first 14 days, indicating that early community operation is not hands-off.
Koerner says a newsletter list does not automatically produce revenue; it must be used effectively.

The AI should not be given unrestricted access without considering what it might do. Koerner says users can set permissions to require approval, block actions, or always allow them, and advises doing their own research.
The host discloses an affiliate link for Beehiiv and promotes a discount code, creating a promotional conflict in his positive platform recommendation.
The transcript suggests using a business's email list for new offers or a local newsletter but does not address list consent, privacy notices, or marketing permissions.
